items.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020
items.q: a Johnny Cash record over here, Nat King Cole over there

ctx.x: Okay. After describing how many CDs you get every year, either physical or on-line, I was going to ask what do you listen to at home, but maybe you don’t want to listen to anything.

Yeah, because I listen in the office a lot. But at home I’ll listen to — sometimes I’ll listen to jazz; sometimes I’ll listen to, you know, rock; sometimes I’ll listen to classical; I love country. I love music. I love music. Jazz is what I do for the living and it’s informed by everything else that I hear. So I’m somebody who you’ll, even in the office people go, “What are you doing in there?” Because I’ll just have a playlist and they’ll go, “What is that?” And you know it’s one hit of bebop, one hit of avante…
If there’s one person, a musician, that you could have interviewed but was gone before, who would you have liked to have been able to sit with? That’s a hard question.
